people_also_ask: Where do Gen Z girls buy clothes?
author: Ash

copy.intro: Maybe your mall's Claire's shut in the 2025 closures, or you went to its website and found a single Disney Villains drop. You still need cheap earrings, and maybe somewhere to get a first piercing. These are the stores to try instead. The piercing studios and Lovisa come first, then the cheap accessories stores, then jewelry brands that cost more but sell gold and sterling silver.

bodies.studs:
Studs is the pick if you'd rather be pierced with a needle than with Claire's hand-pressured device. Its own earrings start low too, and the Mini CZ Stud ($22) is one of its best sellers.

The pricing works differently, though. Claire's pierces free when you buy a starter kit from $29.99. Studs charges for the service, $40 for one hole or $55 for two, and the jewelry comes on top. So a first lobe piercing costs more here. What you get is a single-use sterilized needle. Its studios include Abbot Kinney in Venice, California and Georgetown in Washington, DC.

It only pierces ages 10 and up, so younger kids belong at Rowan. Shipping is free over $75. Fashion jewelry can come back within 21 days, but piercing jewelry can't.
bodies.rowan:
Rowan is where to take a baby or young child for a first piercing. Every piercing is done by a licensed nurse, and the device option starts at 2 months old with a DTaP vaccination.

The service is $35 a piercing, and the earrings cost extra. Device jewelry starts at $60, so a first pair costs well over Claire's $29.99 kit. What that buys is the nurse and the metal: 14K gold, sterling silver, titanium or platinum, and nothing with nickel or brass in it.

After the piercing, the shop is mostly small studs and huggies, like the Bow CZ Huggies ($36). Free shipping starts at $150, the highest bar here alongside Gorjana and Missoma. For a teen getting two holes by needle, Studs comes out cheaper ($55 against Rowan's $70).
bodies.lovisa:
Lovisa is the nearest thing to the Claire's earring wall. Most of its earrings cost under $20, and the 4mm Pearl Stud Earrings are $2.99.

It pierces free the same way Claire's does: buy the stud and the piercing costs nothing. Surgical steel studs start at $34.99, $5 more than Claire's starter kit, and 14KT gold starts at $59.99. Every store does lobes. Nose and helix piercings aren't offered everywhere, so check before you go.

Here's the catch. Earrings can't be returned for a change of mind, online or in store. So buy the pair you're sure about, like the Gold 3D Flower Hoop Earrings ($12.99), rather than a mystery pack. US shipping is free over $45.
bodies.charming-charlie:
Charming Charlie is the one for bright statement earrings, and its full prices run from $16 to $56. The Daisy studs ($16) come in cream, green, pink or purple.

Color is how the whole store is organized, with a Shop By Color menu, and the earrings sit next to handbags, scarves and sunglasses. That helps if you're matching earrings to an outfit rather than buying a single pair.

Nearly every earring is marked down, so the full price is the exception here, and the sale price is what you'll usually pay. Refunds close after 7 days, the shortest window on this list (30 days gets you site credit). Shipping is free over $50.
bodies.ardene:
Ardene is the cheapest way to fill a jewelry box from this list. The 12-Pack Mixed Earrings cost $7.90, and no earring on its US site costs more than $17.90. Plated hoops like the 14K Gold Plated Tubular Hoops are $7.90 too.

It's a Canadian chain that sells clothes, shoes and bags alongside the jewelry, with stores in a handful of US states. The US site charges in dollars. Shipping is free for Ardene Rewards members, or over $60 if you'd rather not sign up.

The trade-off is returns. Earrings can't be returned or exchanged at all, so treat every pack as final. Hot Topic's earrings start at the same $7.90 and can go back within 30 days.
bodies.hot-topic:
Hot Topic is where to go for fandom earrings. Licensed designs fill the section, from the Marvel Captain America Shield Stud Earrings ($7.90) to earring sets like the Cinnamoroll Heart Bling Earring Set ($14.90).

Claire's leans on character tie-ins too. Its only online drop right now is Disney Villains earring stacks. Hot Topic goes much further into anime, games and film, and its RockLove collaborations sit at the top, such as the Avatar The Last Airbender X RockLove Kyoshi Warrior Fan Earrings ($115.90).

Plenty of pairs cost $7.90, about a quarter of Claire's $29.99 stacks. Standard shipping is $7.99 and free over $75. Earrings can come back within 30 days, but body jewelry is final sale.
bodies.forever-21:
Forever 21 has the cheapest single pairs online, if simple metal hoops and drops are what you want. The Etched Hoop Earrings are $6.99, and every full-price pair sits between $5.99 and $6.99, the Faux Pearl Geo Drop Earrings included.

The earring range is small, and almost all of it carries a markdown, so expect to pay the sale price. That makes it an add-on to a clothing order rather than a place to shop for earrings alone. Shipping is free over $50.

Ardene has more earrings at similar prices. Forever 21's edge is returns: 30 days, while Ardene takes no earrings back. Clearance pieces are final here, though.
bodies.little-words-project:
Little Words Project is a bracelet brand first. Its earrings are a short list, led by the Breathe Puffy Huggies ($38).

The draw is the beaded word bracelets. You pick a word, wear it, then pass it on and track where it goes. The earrings work as a match for those, like the Blessed Scalloped Bezel Studs ($48). It has stores in malls such as King of Prussia and Roosevelt Field, plus a shop at Disney Springs.

There are only three earrings, all pricier than Claire's $29.99 stacks. If earrings are the main buy, Lovisa has thousands. Returns take 30 days, and US shipping is free over $60.
bodies.astrid-miyu:
Astrid & Miyu is the one for adults who want a piercing and new earrings in the same visit. Its Bold Medium Hoops in Gold cost $110.

It's a London brand with US stores in Los Angeles and New York, including one inside Bloomingdale's on 59th Street, and you can book piercing or permanent jewelry there. Online, the cheapest piece is a $35 titanium piercing post. The middle of the earring range sits around $125.

US delivery is free, and returns are free within 28 days. Pieces bought as a set have to go back as the whole set. For gold earrings at a lower start price, Gorjana's single studs begin at $30.
bodies.gorjana:
Gorjana is the step up to gold without jumping straight to fine-jewelry prices. Its single studs start at $30, the Bee Single Stud among them.

Selling singles is the useful part. Once a second or third hole has healed, you can add one stud at a time instead of buying a pair, all the way up to 14K gold like the Crew Single Huggie 8mm ($150). It's a California brand with stores around the US, and buying online to pick up in store is free.

Prices climb fast past that, and the diamond studs go over $1,000. Standard shipping is $8 unless you spend $150. Unworn pieces can come back within 30 days.
bodies.missoma:
Missoma is for when you'd rather pay more for 18k gold vermeil or sterling silver. The Bar Stud Earrings in sterling silver cost $65, the same as its Pave Initial Single Stud Earring in gold vermeil.

It's a London demi-fine brand, and the hoops are a good place to start. The Chubby Oval Medium Hoop Earrings are $122 in 18k gold plating. Returns run 90 days, the longest window on this list, which matters when a pair costs this much.

It's also the priciest pick, with collaboration pieces reaching $9,282, and shipping is only free over $150. Gorjana starts lower for a similar gold look, and Lovisa costs a fraction of either.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body:
Start with who's getting pierced. Rowan's nurses pierce from 2 months old, Studs uses a needle from age 10, and Lovisa pierces free when you buy a stud, the same deal Claire's offers.

For earrings alone, the budget does the sorting. Ardene and Forever 21 stay under $18, Lovisa never passes $50, and Hot Topic is the place for licensed characters. Charming Charlie covers bold color in between. If you want gold or sterling silver that costs more, Gorjana lets you buy one stud at a time, while Astrid & Miyu and Missoma start at $35 and $65.

Check returns before a cheap haul. Lovisa and Ardene won't take earrings back.

faqs.q: Is Claire's going out of business?
faqs.a: No. Claire's filed for bankruptcy in August 2025 and announced hundreds of US store closures, but Ames Watson Capital bought its North American business that September, and its store locator still lists stores across the US.
faqs.source_query: is claire's going out of business

faqs.q: How much is it to get your ears pierced at Claire's?
faqs.a: The piercing itself is free when you buy a starter kit. Kits start at $29.99 in medical-grade stainless steel, and gold and diamond kits cost more. Lovisa works the same way, with studs from $34.99.
faqs.source_query: how much is it to get your ears pierced at claire's

faqs.a: Yes, but only at select stores. Every Claire's does lobe piercings, while nose and cartilage piercings depend on the location, so check the store locator first. Nose studs start at $59.99.

It was Icing, a Claire's chain aimed at older teens and young women. Claire's discontinued it in August 2025, and icing.com now sends you to claires.com. Astrid & Miyu is the nearest grown-up alternative here.
